6386.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂er-dʰrom, from *h₂er- (“to fit”) + *-dʰrom (“tool or instrument suffix”), synchronically analyzable as ἀραρίσκω (ararískō) + -θρον (-thron).

6370.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂(e)rmós, from the root *h₂er- (“to fit together, join”), whence also ἀραρίσκω (ararískō, “join, fit together”).

6376.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂éḱmō. Cognates include Sanskrit अश्म॑न् (áśman), Avestan 𐬀𐬐𐬨𐬀𐬥 (akman), Old English hamor (English hammer), and Lithuanian akmuõ.

6369.t: From *ἁρμων (*harmōn) + -ία (-ía). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to join, fit, fix together”).

6334.t: From ἀποφθέγγομαι (apophthéngomai, “I plainly speak my mind”), from ἀπο- (apo-, “away”) + φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to speak loudly”), + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

6346.t: From ἄσωτος (ắsōtos, “having no hope of safety”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā).

6392.t: From an earlier *ἄϝεθλον (*áwethlon), traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁- (“to blow (of wind)”) + *-dʰlom (forms nouns denoting tool or instrument), as if "gasp, pant, wheeze", if not from a similar root meaning "to strive".

6332.t: From ἀποδίδωμι (apodídōmi) + -σις (-sis). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀢𐀉𐀯 (a-pu-du-si).

6367.t: From ἁλής (hālḗs, “thronged, crowded”) + -ίζω (-ízō), from Proto-Indo-European *wel- (“to push, press”).

6385.t: Contracted from ἀέρδην (aérdēn), from the root of ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift”) + -δην (-dēn, deverbal adverb suffix).

6352.t: ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + τειχίζω (teikhĭ́zō, to wall) + -τος (-tos, verbal adjective suffix)

6383.t: Commonly derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éntm̥, accusative singular of *h₂énts. Alternatively, Dunkel suggests a 'directive' *h₂ént-o from the same root noun, with subsequent alpha harmony in Greek.

6300.t: From ἄπληστος (áplēstos, “insatiable, greedy”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix), ultimately from πίμπλημι (pímplēmi, “to fill”).

6371.t: From ἀγρός (ăgrós) + οἰκέω (oikéō). For the opposition with ἀστεῖος (ăsteîos), compare typologically Latin agrestis (cognate via Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros), pāgānus, rūsticus vs. cīvīlis, urbānus.

6380.t: Probably cognate with ἄκρος (ắkros), but Beekes considers this uncertain.

6387.t: From ἀ- (a-, privative alpha) + ῥώννυμι (rhṓnnumi, “to strengthen”) + -τος (-tos).

6372.t: Generally considered to be a perfect participle of verb ἄγω (ắgō, “to lead”), but without the reduplication.

6365.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + χρεία (khreía, “need; use”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

6339.t: The word is of Iranian origin (see Old North Iranian *ṛdba-, Old Persian *ṛdva-) and ultimately from Akkadian 𒅈𒁕𒁉 (/⁠ardabu⁠/, “capacity measure of about 56 litres”), found as Aramaic 𐡀𐡓𐡃𐡁 (ʾrdb) / אַרְדְּבָא (ʾardəḇā) / ܐܪܕܒܐ (ʾardəḇā), (Classical Syriac…

6336.t: From ἄργυρος (ắrgŭros, “silver”) + κόπτω (kóptō, “to strike; to cut”).

6356.t: From ἀφαιρέω (aphairéō, “I take away”) + -σις (-sis, nominal suffix), from ἀφ’ (aph’, apocopic form of ἀπό (apó, “from”)) + αἱρέω (hairéō, “I take”).

6335.t: Probably from Ἀραβία (Arăbĭ́ā, “Arabia”) + -ις (-is), after its native environment. For the formation compare ἰβηρίς (ibērís, “pepperwort”).

6378.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + κριτός (krĭtós, “chosen, picked out, separated”).

6384.t: From the same substrate root as ἄπιον (ắpĭon, “pear”) and Latin pirum (“pear”).

6342.t: From ἀρχιτέκτων (arkhitéktōn, “architect, master craftsman”) + -ία (-ía), from ἀρχι- (arkhi-, “master”) + τέκτων (téktōn, “craftsman, builder”).

6375.t: From ἆθλος (âthlos, “conflict, struggle”) + -ιος (-ios, “a suffix added to nouns or adjectives, forming adjectives: pertaining to, belonging to”)

6382.t: From ἀμφι- (ămphĭ-, “on both sides”) + ὁδός (hodós, “way; path”).

6358.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + φορολογέω (phorologéō, “to levy tribute from”) + -τος (-tos).
